subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure under the dilation η_{x,λ}
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and η = η_{x,λ}. Then (i) Hⁿ(η(s)) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·Hⁿ(s) for every s ⊆ ℝ^P, and (ii) the push-forward measure satisfies η_#Hⁿ = ofReal(λⁿ)·Hⁿ (i.e. Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) = λⁿHⁿ(B) for every Borel B), where Hⁿ = μHE[n].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → (∀ s : Set (Euclid P), μHE[n] (dilation x lam '' s) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) * μHE[n] s) ∧ Measure.map (dilation x lam) (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam ^ n) • (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 0(i); Hⁿ is Mathlib's normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure μHE[n]. Here η = η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz.
1. For every s ⊆ ℝ^P, η(s) = τ(λ⁻¹·s), where λ⁻¹·s = {λ⁻¹y : y ∈ s} and τ(z) := −λ⁻¹x + z, because η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y.
2. τ is an isometry of ℝ^P (a translation), and Hausdorff measures are invariant under isometries (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image): Hⁿ(τ(E)) = Hⁿ(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P. Hence Hⁿ(η(s)) = Hⁿ(λ⁻¹·s).
3. Homogeneity: for r ≠ 0 and every E ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(r·E) = |r|ⁿ·Hⁿ(E) (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀: μHE[d](r • E) = ‖r‖₊^d • μHE[d](E); the map y ↦ ry multiplies the diameter of every covering set by |r|, so every δ-approximating sum for Hⁿ is multiplied by |r|ⁿ). With r = λ⁻¹ > 0 the factor is (λ⁻¹)ⁿ = λ^{−n}, which as an element of [0,∞] is ofReal(λ^{−n}). With step 2 this proves (i): Hⁿ(η(s)) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·Hⁿ(s) for every s ⊆ ℝ^P.
4. Proof of (ii). η is continuous, hence Borel measurable, so (η_#Hⁿ)(B) = Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) for every Borel B. Since η is a bijection with inverse ι(z) = x + λz, η⁻¹(B) = ι(B). Moreover ι = η_{x',λ'} with x' := −λ⁻¹x and λ' := λ⁻¹ > 0, because η_{x',λ'}(z) = −λ'⁻¹x' + λ'⁻¹z = −λ·(−λ⁻¹x) + λz = x + λz. By (i) applied to (x', λ'), Hⁿ(ι(B)) = ofReal(λ'^{−n})·Hⁿ(B) = ofReal(λⁿ)·Hⁿ(B). Thus η_#Hⁿ and ofReal(λⁿ)·Hⁿ agree on all Borel sets and are therefore equal measures (Measure.ext). This holds for every n, including n = 0. ∎
Formalization notes (this exact statement was proved in a scratch build): with `open scoped Pointwise`, η '' s = (fun z => −(λ⁻¹ • x) + z) '' (λ⁻¹ • s) by image_smul and image_image; isometry_add_left; ENNReal.smul_def, ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal, abs_of_pos; for (ii) Measure.ext, Measure.map_apply, Measure.smul_apply and the set identity dilation x λ ⁻¹' s = dilation (−(λ⁻¹ • x)) λ⁻¹ '' s, then (i) for (−(λ⁻¹ • x), λ⁻¹) and inv_inv.
proof_key_steps: η(s) is a translate of λ⁻¹·s; Hⁿ is invariant under translations (isometries).
Hⁿ(r·E) = |r|ⁿHⁿ(E) (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀) with r = λ⁻¹ gives (i).
η⁻¹(B) = η_{−λ⁻¹x,λ⁻¹}(B), so (i) for the inverse dilation gives (η_#Hⁿ)(B) = λⁿHⁿ(B) on Borel sets, hence (ii).

audit.reason: Both factors are correct: image measure scales by λ⁻ⁿ, while the mapped measure scales by λⁿ. Translation invariance and homogeneity prove the first clause for arbitrary sets; applying that established clause to the inverse dilation proves the second without circularity.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent spaces are invariant under dilations
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, x, y ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P and η = η_{x,λ}. If Q is the approximate tangent space of M at y in the sense of Simon 3.1.4 (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{y,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P)), then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (η(M)) (η(y)) Q.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x y : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < lam → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (dilation x lam '' M) (dilation x lam y) Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–86), formalized by SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q := finrank Q = n ∧ ∀ f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ), lim_{r→0+} ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' M} f dHⁿ = ∫_Q f dHⁿ, with blowUpMap y r w = r⁻¹•(w − y); parent proof step 2, orientation bullet (η_{z,r}(η(M)) = η_{y,λr}(M)). Here η = η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, Hⁿ = μHE[n].
1. The condition finrank Q = n involves neither M nor the base point, so it holds for η(M) at η(y).
2. Set identity. For w ∈ ℝ^P, η(w) − η(y) = (−λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹w) − (−λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y) = λ⁻¹(w − y). Hence for every r ∈ ℝ, blowUpMap(η(y), r)(η(w)) = r⁻¹λ⁻¹(w − y) = (λr)⁻¹(w − y) = blowUpMap(y, λr)(w), using (λr)⁻¹ = λ⁻¹r⁻¹ (valid in ℝ with the convention 0⁻¹ = 0). Taking images of M: blowUpMap(η(y), r)(η(M)) = blowUpMap(y, λr)(M) for all r.
3. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ) and put g(s) := ∫_{blowUpMap(y,s)(M)} f dHⁿ. By step 2, for every r the integral ∫_{blowUpMap(η(y),r)(η(M))} f dHⁿ is literally g(λr) (same domain of integration, same integrand and same measure, so no integrability is needed for this identity).
4. The map r ↦ λr sends the filter r → 0+ into the filter s → 0+: it is continuous with value 0 at 0, and λr > 0 whenever r > 0 because λ > 0. By hypothesis g(s) → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as s → 0+. Composing the two limits, ∫_{blowUpMap(η(y),r)(η(M))} f dHⁿ = g(λr) → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0+.
5. Steps 1 and 4 are exactly HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (η(M)) (η(y)) Q. ∎
Formalization notes (this exact statement was proved in a scratch build): obtain ⟨hdim, hconv⟩; prove the set identity with image_image, congr, funext and the rewrite chain ← smul_sub, smul_smul, mul_inv, mul_comm, sub_sub_sub_cancel_right (after writing dilation x λ y = λ⁻¹ • (y − x)); simp_rw it; the filter limit by tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within with mul_pos; conclude with (hconv f).comp.
proof_key_steps: η(w) − η(y) = λ⁻¹(w − y), hence η_{η(y),r}(η(M)) = η_{y,λr}(M) for every r.
The rescaled integrals for η(M) at η(y) at scale r equal those for M at y at scale λr.
r ↦ λr maps r → 0+ to s → 0+, so the limit transfers; dim Q = n is unchanged.

subproblem.title: Test forms correspond under η_{x,λ}, and η_{x,λ#}T(ω) = λ^{−n}T(ω∘η)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary subset, x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and η = η_{x,λ} (η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x), Contract `dilation x λ`). Then (a) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) there is ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y ∈ ℝ^P; (b) for every ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) there is ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y; (c) for every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y, the blow-up satisfies η_{x,λ#}T(ω) = λ^{−n}·T(ω'). Here 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n and η_{x,λ#}T = blowUp T x λ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam), (∀ ω : TestFormOn (dilation x lam '' U) n, ∃ ω' : TestFormOn U n, ∀ y : Euclid P, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (dilation x lam y)) ∧ (∀ ω' : TestFormOn U n, ∃ ω : TestFormOn (dilation x lam '' U) n, ∀ y : Euclid P, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (dilation x lam y)) ∧ ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn (dilation x lam '' U) n) (ω' : TestFormOn U n), (∀ y : Euclid P, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (dilation x lam y)) → blowUp T x lam hlam.ne' ω = lam⁻¹ ^ n * T ω'
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 0(ii) (pullback by η_{x,λ}); Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 (push-forward f_#T(ω) = T(f^#ω), chapter-06.txt lines 405–418).
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. For V ⊆ ℝ^P (any subset), 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n is the set of C^∞ maps ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (n-covectors) with compact topological support tsupport ω ⊆ V; elements of 𝒟ⁿ(V) are determined by their underlying forms. η_#Y := η_{x,λ#}Y = blowUp Y x λ for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U). By the Contract definition of blowUp, for T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) we have η_#T(ω) = T(ν), where ν ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has underlying form ν(y) = ω(−λ⁻¹x + L y) ∘ L with L := λ⁻¹·id (= dilationCLM P λ), i.e. ν(y)(v₁,…,vₙ) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) (SimonGMT affinePullbackForm L (−λ⁻¹x) ω; it is a test form in η⁻¹(η(U)) and is regarded as a test form in U through the inclusion η⁻¹(η(U)) ⊆ U, which does not change the underlying form).
1. η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι. Indeed η is the composition of y ↦ λ⁻¹y (a homeomorphism since λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) with the translation z ↦ z − λ⁻¹x, and η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z, ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y. Both η and ι are affine, hence C^∞. In particular η is injective, so η⁻¹(η(V)) = V for every V ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. Two facts about supports. Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be continuous and f : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P). (i) tsupport(f∘h) ⊆ h⁻¹(tsupport f): the set h⁻¹(tsupport f) is closed and contains {f∘h ≠ 0} = h⁻¹{f ≠ 0}. (ii) If h is a homeomorphism and f has compact support, then f∘h has compact support: h⁻¹(tsupport f) is compact (it is the image of the compact set tsupport f under the continuous inverse of h), and tsupport(f∘h) is a closed subset of it by (i).
3. Proof of (a). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) and put ω' := ω∘η. Then ω' is C^∞ (composition of C^∞ maps), has compact support by 2(ii), and tsupport ω' ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U by 2(i) and step 1. Hence ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y by definition.
4. Proof of (b). Let ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and put ω := ω'∘ι. Then ω is C^∞, has compact support by 2(ii) (ι is a homeomorphism), and tsupport ω ⊆ ι⁻¹(tsupport ω') ⊆ ι⁻¹(U). If ι(z) ∈ U then z = η(ι(z)) ∈ η(U); hence tsupport ω ⊆ η(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). Finally ω(η(y)) = ω'(ι(η(y))) = ω'(y) for every y.
5. Proof of (c). Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) and ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y, and let ν be the test form in the definition of η_#T(ω). Note −λ⁻¹x + L y = η(y). Fix y and v₁,…,vₙ ∈ ℝ^P and put α := ω(η(y)) ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P). Since α is multilinear, α(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) = (∏_{i=1}^{n} λ⁻¹)·α(v₁,…,vₙ) = λ^{−n}·α(v₁,…,vₙ) (for n = 0 the empty product is 1 = λ⁰). Hence ν(y) = λ^{−n}ω(η(y)) = λ^{−n}ω'(y) for all y, so ν = λ^{−n}ω' as elements of 𝒟ⁿ(U). By linearity of T, η_#T(ω) = T(ν) = T(λ^{−n}ω') = λ^{−n}·T(ω'). Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. 4. (iv) Let T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟^m(η(U)). By definition ∂Y(φ) = Y(dφ). Then ∂(η_#T)(ω) = η_#T(dω) = T(ν_{dω}) and η_#(∂T)(ω) = ∂T(ν_ω) = T(dν_ω), where the inclusion into 𝒟(U) does not change underlying forms. subproblem.title: Mass scaling of blow-ups: M_{η(W)}(η_{x,λ#}T) = λ^{−n}M_W(T)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0, η = η_{x,λ}, and let W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary. Source: parent proof step 1; scaling identity (1) in the proof of Simon 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 329–331); mass M_W of Simon 6.2.5 (SimonGMT massOn with the Euclidean coefficient norm).
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. For a current Y with domain V and W ⊆ ℝ^P put Adm(V,W) := {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) : tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y} (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm; massAdmissibleOn V n W), so M_W(Y) = sup{ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ Adm(V,W)} ∈ [0,∞]. Put S := η_#T and c := λ^{−n} ≥ 0.
1. Facts on η: η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι: η is y ↦ λ⁻¹y (a homeomorphism, λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) followed by the translation z ↦ z − λ⁻¹x, η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z and ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y. In particular η is injective and η⁻¹(η(W)) = W. For continuous h and any f, tsupport(f∘h) ⊆ h⁻¹(tsupport f), since h⁻¹(tsupport f) is closed and contains {f∘h ≠ 0} = h⁻¹{f ≠ 0}.
2. Upper bound. Let ω ∈ Adm(η(U), η(W)). By testform_correspondence (a) choose ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y. Then ω' ∈ Adm(U,W): since ω' = ω∘η, tsupport ω' ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(W)) = W, and |ω'(y)| = |ω(η(y))| ≤ 1. By testform_correspondence (c), S(ω) = c·T(ω'). As c ≥ 0, ofReal(S(ω)) = ofReal(c·T(ω')) = ofReal(c)·ofReal(T(ω')) ≤ ofReal(c)·M_W(T). Taking the supremum over ω gives M_{η(W)}(S) ≤ ofReal(c)·M_W(T).
3. Lower bound. Multiplication by a fixed element of [0,∞] commutes with suprema (ENNReal.mul_sSup), so ofReal(c)·M_W(T) = sup{ofReal(c)·ofReal(T(ω')) : ω' ∈ Adm(U,W)}. Let ω' ∈ Adm(U,W). By testform_correspondence (b) choose ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y. For every z, ω(z) = ω(η(ι(z))) = ω'(ι(z)), i.e. ω = ω'∘ι; hence tsupport ω ⊆ ι⁻¹(tsupport ω') ⊆ ι⁻¹(W) ⊆ η(W) (if ι(z) ∈ W then z = η(ι(z)) ∈ η(W)), and |ω(z)| = |ω'(ι(z))| ≤ 1. subproblem.title: Push-forward of an integer multiplicity representation by η_{x,λ}
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0, η = η_{x,λ}, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation (IMRep) of T in U. Then there is an IMRep R' of η_{x,λ#}T in η(U) such that μ_{R'}(B) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·μ_R(η⁻¹(B)) for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P, where μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (IMRep.measure).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → ∃ R' : IMRep (dilation x lam '' U) n, R'.Represents (blowUp T x lam hlam.ne') ∧ ∀ s : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet s → R'.measure s = ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) * R.measure (dilation x lam ⁻¹' s)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 2; Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9 (push-forward of an integer multiplicity current by a Lipschitz map, Lemma 3.9; chapter-06.txt lines 770–862), specialized to the similarity η, whose Jacobian is the constant λ^{−n}, so that the area formula reduces to the scaling of Hⁿ; Simon Ch. 3, Definitions 1.1 and 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 12–16, 77–86).
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. For V ⊆ ℝ^P (any subset), 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n is the set of C^∞ maps ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (n-covectors) with compact topological support tsupport ω ⊆ V; elements of 𝒟ⁿ(V) are determined by their underlying forms. η_#Y := η_{x,λ#}Y = blowUp Y x λ for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Hⁿ = μHE[n] and c := ofReal(λ^{−n}) ∈ (0,∞). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U consists of a Borel set M ⊆ U that is countably n-rectifiable, a measurable θ : ℝ^P → ℕ with θ > 0 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and ξ : ℝ^P → Λₙ(ℝ^P), a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, such that for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q. R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y); R represents T iff T(ω) = R.action(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); μ_R = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density θ (IMRep.measure).
1. η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι: η is y ↦ λ⁻¹y (a homeomorphism, λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) followed by the translation z ↦ z − λ⁻¹x, η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z and ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y. Hence η is a measurable embedding (a Borel isomorphism of ℝ^P): η maps Borel sets onto Borel sets, η⁻¹(η(s)) = s and η(η⁻¹(t)) = t for all sets s, t.
2. Key identity: for every Borel s, Hⁿ⌞η(s) = c·η_#(Hⁿ⌞s). Proof: for a measurable embedding η, every measure ν and every set t, (η_#ν)⌞t = η_#(ν⌞η⁻¹(t)) (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map). With ν = Hⁿ and t = η(s): η_#(Hⁿ⌞s) = (η_#Hⁿ)⌞η(s) = (ofReal(λⁿ)·Hⁿ)⌞η(s) = ofReal(λⁿ)·(Hⁿ⌞η(s)) by hausdorff_scaling (ii). Since c·ofReal(λⁿ) = ofReal(λ^{−n}λⁿ) = 1, multiplying by c gives the claim. Consequences, for Borel s:
 (A) for g : ℝ^P → [0,∞], ∫_{η(s)} g dHⁿ = c·∫_s g∘η dHⁿ (lintegral against a scalar multiple of a measure, and MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map, which needs no measurability of g);
 (B) for g : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{η(s)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n}·∫_s g∘η dHⁿ for the Bochner integral (integral_smul_measure with c.toReal = λ^{−n}, and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, which holds for every g, integrable or not);
 (C) if a property q satisfies q(η(y)) for Hⁿ⌞s-a.e. y, then q holds Hⁿ⌞η(s)-a.e. (MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff; a ν-null set is (c·ν)-null);
 (D) if h∘η is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞s, then h is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞η(s) (MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff and AEStronglyMeasurable.smul_measure).
3. Definition of R' and verification of the IMRep conditions in η(U). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) represent T and put M' := η(M), θ' := θ∘ι, ξ' := ξ∘ι; then θ'(η(y)) = θ(y) and ξ'(η(y)) = ξ(y).
 (a) M' is Borel by step 1, and M' ⊆ η(U) since M ⊆ U.
 (b) M' is countably n-rectifiable: choose M₀ with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) (Simon 3.1.1, SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable). Then Hⁿ(η(M₀)) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·0 = 0 by hausdorff_scaling (i); each η∘F_j is Lipschitz, since η is the linear map λ⁻¹·id (Lipschitz with constant ‖λ⁻¹·id‖) followed by a translation (an isometry); and M' ⊆ η(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j (η∘F_j)(ℝⁿ), because y ∈ M₀ gives η(y) ∈ η(M₀) and y = F_j(v) gives η(y) = (η∘F_j)(v).
 (c) θ' is measurable (θ is measurable and ι is continuous) and ℕ-valued; for z = η(y) ∈ M' with y ∈ M, θ'(z) = θ(y) > 0.
 (d) Local integrability: let K ⊆ η(U) be compact. Then M' ∩ K = η(M ∩ η⁻¹(K)) (f(s ∩ f⁻¹(t)) = f(s) ∩ t for every map f; Set.image_inter_preimage), and M ∩ η⁻¹(K) is Borel (K is closed). By 2(A), ∫_{M'∩K} θ' dHⁿ = c·∫_{M∩η⁻¹(K)} θ'∘η dHⁿ = c·∫_{M∩η⁻¹(K)} θ dHⁿ. The set η⁻¹(K) is compact (η is a homeomorphism) and η⁻¹(K) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U, so the last integral is finite by the local integrability of R; as c < ∞ the product is finite.
 (e) ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M' by 2(D), because ξ'∘η = ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M.
 (f) Orientation: let p(z) be the statement “∃Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' z Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(z)) Q”. For Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q; for such y the sibling tangent_invariance gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (η(M)) (η(y)) Q, and ξ'(η(y)) = ξ(y), so p(η(y)) holds. Hence p∘η holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., and by 2(C) p holds Hⁿ⌞M'-a.e.
 Therefore R' := (M', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in η(U).
4. R' represents η_#T. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). By testform_correspondence (a) choose ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y; by testform_correspondence (c) and since R represents T, η_#T(ω) = λ^{−n}T(ω') = λ^{−n}R.action(ω') = λ^{−n}∫_M θ(y)ξ(y)(ω(η(y))) dHⁿ(y). On the other hand, by 2(B) with s = M and g(z) := θ'(z)·ξ'(z)(ω(z)), R'.action(ω) = ∫_{η(M)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_M g(η(y)) dHⁿ(y) = λ^{−n}∫_M θ(y)ξ(y)(ω(η(y))) dHⁿ(y). The two expressions agree, so R'.Represents(η_#T).
5. Measure identity. Let B be Borel; then η⁻¹(B) is Borel and
 μ_{R'}(B) = ∫_B θ' d(Hⁿ⌞M') (density formula on the measurable set B)
 = c·∫_B θ' d(η_#(Hⁿ⌞M)) (step 2)
 = c·∫_{η⁻¹(B)} θ'∘η d(Hⁿ⌞M) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map and MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map)
 = c·∫_{η⁻¹(B)} θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = c·μ_R(η⁻¹(B)),
 i.e. μ_{R'}(B) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·μ_R(η⁻¹(B)). No hypothesis on U or n was used. ∎
Formalization notes (this exact statement was proved in a scratch build from the three siblings' exact types): define R' by the structure literal {carrier := dilation x λ '' R.carrier, mult := fun z => R.mult (x + λ • z), orient := fun z => R.orient (x + λ • z), …}; the measurable embedding is Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding of (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ⁻¹ _).trans (Homeomorph.addLeft (−(λ⁻¹ • x))), whose coercion is dilation x λ; prove the restriction identity hkey once (Measure.restrict_smul, the sibling's map identity, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, preimage_image_eq, smul_smul); Lipschitz constant via ((isometry_add_left (−(λ⁻¹ • x))).lipschitzWith.comp (dilationCLM P λ).lipschitzWith).comp hK; local integrability via image_inter_preimage, lintegral_smul_measure, MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map, ENNReal.mul_ne_top; representation via integral_smul_measure, MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal; measure via withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_smul, lintegral_smul_measure, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map; orientation via Measure.ae_smul_measure and MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff.
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ⌞η(s) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·η_#(Hⁿ⌞s) for Borel s (restrict_map for the measurable embedding η and hausdorff_scaling (ii)); hence change of variables for lintegrals, Bochner integrals, a.e. statements and a.e. strong measurability.

R' := (η(M), θ∘ι, ξ∘ι): Borel, contained in η(U), countably n-rectifiable (η(M₀) null, η∘F_j Lipschitz), positive integer multiplicity, locally integrable (η⁻¹(K) compact in U), measurable orientation, and orienting approximate tangent planes a.e. by tangent_invariance.
Represents: η_#T(ω) = λ^{−n}T(ω∘η) = λ^{−n}∫_M θ ξ(ω∘η) dHⁿ = ∫_{η(M)} θ' ξ'(ω) dHⁿ.
Measure: μ_{R'}(B) = ofReal(λ^{−n})∫_{η⁻¹(B)} θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = ofReal(λ^{−n})μ_R(η⁻¹(B)).

subproblem.title: Every current in η(U) is a blow-up of a current in U, preserving integer multiplicity
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and η = η_{x,λ}. For every S' ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)) there is S'' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with η_{x,λ#}S'' = S', and S'' is integer multiplicity whenever S' is.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam) (S' : GeometricCurrentOn (dilation x lam '' U) n), ∃ S'' : GeometricCurrentOn U n, blowUp S'' x lam hlam.ne' = S' ∧ (IsIntegerMultiplicity S' → IsIntegerMultiplicity S'')
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 3(a), 3(b); Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 and Lemma 3.9 (push-forward of integer multiplicity currents; chapter-06.txt lines 405–418 and 770–862), applied to the inverse similarity η⁻¹.
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. For V ⊆ ℝ^P (any subset), 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n is the set of C^∞ maps ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (n-covectors) with compact topological support tsupport ω ⊆ V; elements of 𝒟ⁿ(V) are determined by their underlying forms. η_#Y := η_{x,λ#}Y = blowUp Y x λ for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U).
1. Let x' := −λ⁻¹x, λ' := λ⁻¹ > 0 and κ := η_{x',λ'}. Then κ(z) = −λ'⁻¹x' + λ'⁻¹z = −λ·(−λ⁻¹x) + λz = x + λz = ι(z). Since η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z and ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y, we get η∘κ = id and κ∘η = id, and V := κ(η(U)) = U (every u ∈ U equals κ(η(u)), and κ(η(u)) = u for u ∈ U).
2. Definition of S''. Let S' ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)). The blow-up κ_#S' := η_{x',λ'#}S' is a current in κ(η(U)) = V. Since U ⊆ V (step 1), define S'' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) by S''(ω') := κ_#S'(ω') for ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where ω' is regarded as an element of 𝒟ⁿ(V) with the same underlying form (restriction of the domain, SimonGMT restrictDomain, which preserves linearity and sequential continuity).
3. η_#S'' = S'. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). By testform_correspondence (a) (for U, x, λ) choose ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y; by testform_correspondence (c), η_#S''(ω) = λ^{−n}S''(ω') = λ^{−n}κ_#S'(ω'). Now apply testform_correspondence (c) to the domain η(U), the current S', the point x' and λ' > 0, the test form ω' regarded in 𝒟ⁿ(κ(η(U))) and the test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)): its hypothesis ω(z) = ω'(κ(z)) for all z holds because ω'(κ(z)) = ω(η(κ(z))) = ω(z). Hence κ_#S'(ω') = λ'^{−n}S'(ω) = λⁿS'(ω), and η_#S''(ω) = λ^{−n}λⁿS'(ω) = S'(ω). As ω was arbitrary, η_{x,λ#}S'' = S'.
4. Integer multiplicity. Suppose S' is integer multiplicity, represented by an IMRep R₁ in η(U). By rep_pushforward (applied to the set η(U), the current S', the point x', λ' > 0 and R₁) there is an IMRep R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) in κ(η(U)) = V representing κ_#S'. Since V = U, the same data form an IMRep in U: M₂ ⊆ V = U, every compact K ⊆ U satisfies K ⊆ V so the local integrability condition transfers, and the remaining conditions do not involve the domain. This IMRep represents S'': for ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), S''(ω') = κ_#S'(ω') = R₂.action(ω'), the action depending only on the underlying form. Hence S'' is integer multiplicity. ∎
Formalization notes (this exact statement was proved in a scratch build from the two siblings' exact types): take S'' := (blowUp S' (−(λ⁻¹ • x)) λ⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr hlam).ne').restrictDomain hUV with hUV : U ⊆ dilation (−(λ⁻¹ • x)) λ⁻¹ '' (dilation x λ '' U) obtained from hdom : dilation (−(λ⁻¹ • x)) λ⁻¹ '' (dilation x λ '' U) = U (image_image); prove η_#S'' = S' by GeometricCurrentOn.ext, the sibling's evaluation formula twice, GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply, testFormOnInclusion_coe, inv_inv, mul_pow, inv_mul_cancel₀; the IMRep in U is ⟨R₂.carrier, R₂.mult, R₂.orient, R₂.measurableSet_carrier, R₂.carrier_subset.trans hdom.subset, R₂.rectifiable, R₂.measurable_mult, R₂.mult_pos, fun K hK hKU => R₂.locallyIntegrable_mult K hK (hKU.trans hUV), R₂.aestronglyMeasurable_orient, R₂.orients⟩, representing S'' by fun ω => hR₂ (testFormOnInclusion hUV n ω).
proof_key_steps: The inverse of η is the dilation κ = η_{−λ⁻¹x, λ⁻¹}, so κ(η(U)) = U.
S'' := κ_#S' restricted to U; two applications of testform_correspondence (c) give η_#S''(ω) = λ^{−n}λⁿS'(ω) = S'(ω).
If S' is integer multiplicity, rep_pushforward for κ gives an IMRep of κ_#S' in κ(η(U)) = U, which represents S''.

subproblem.title: Dilations preserve minimality: η_{x,λ#}T is minimizing in η(A)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, A ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0. If T is minimizing in A (Simon 7.1.1 as formalized by IsMinimizingIn), then η_{x,λ#}T is minimizing in η_{x,λ}(A).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam), IsMinimizingIn T A → IsMinimizingIn (blowUp T x lam hlam.ne') (dilation x lam '' A)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3; Simon 7.1.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 12–17); invariance of minimality under dilations as used in the proof of Simon 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 325–333).
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. For V ⊆ ℝ^P (any subset), 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n is the set of C^∞ maps ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (n-covectors) with compact topological support tsupport ω ⊆ V; elements of 𝒟ⁿ(V) are determined by their underlying forms. η_#Y := η_{x,λ#}Y = blowUp Y x λ for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U). IsMinimizingIn T A means: T is integer multiplicity, and M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) whenever W is open with W ⊂⊂ U (closure W compact and ⊆ U), S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary S T holds (∂S = ∂T if n ≥ 1, no condition if n = 0), spt(S − T) is compact and spt(S − T) ⊆ A ∩ W.
1. η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι: η is y ↦ λ⁻¹y (a homeomorphism, λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) followed by the translation z ↦ z − λ⁻¹x, η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z and ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y. In particular η is injective and surjective, η⁻¹(η(E)) = E and η(η⁻¹(E)) = E for all E, preimages of open sets are open, η⁻¹(closure E) = closure(η⁻¹(E)), and preimages of compact sets are compact.
2. η_#T is integer multiplicity: T is integer multiplicity, represented by some IMRep R; by rep_pushforward, η_#T is represented by some IMRep R'.
3. Let W' be open with W' ⊂⊂ η(U), and let S' ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)) be integer multiplicity with SameBoundary S' (η_#T), spt(S' − η_#T) compact and spt(S' − η_#T) ⊆ η(A) ∩ W'. By blowup_preimage choose S'' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with η_#S'' = S' and S'' integer multiplicity.
4. Let W := η⁻¹(W'). Then W is open, and closure W = η⁻¹(closure W') is compact and contained in η⁻¹(η(U)) = U; so W ⊂⊂ U.
5. SameBoundary S'' T. If n = 0 this holds by definition. If n = m + 1, then by blowup_structure (iv), η_#(∂S'') = ∂(η_#S'') = ∂S' = ∂(η_#T) = η_#(∂T), and by blowup_structure (ii) (injectivity in degree m), ∂S'' = ∂T.
6. Support. By blowup_structure (i), S' − η_#T = η_#S'' − η_#T = η_#(S'' − T), and by blowup_structure (iii), spt(S' − η_#T) = η(spt(S'' − T)). Hence spt(S'' − T) = η⁻¹(spt(S' − η_#T)) (η injective), which is compact (step 1) and contained in η⁻¹(η(A) ∩ W') = η⁻¹(η(A)) ∩ η⁻¹(W') = A ∩ W.
7. By the minimality of T applied to W and S'' (steps 3–6), M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S'').
8. Since η is surjective, η(W) = W'. By mass_scaling applied to T and to S'', M_{W'}(η_#T) = M_{η(W)}(η_#T) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·M_W(T) ≤ ofReal(λ^{−n})·M_W(S'') = M_{η(W)}(η_#S'') = M_{W'}(S'), using monotonicity of multiplication in [0,∞].
9. By steps 2–8, η_{x,λ#}T is minimizing in η(A). No hypothesis on U or n was used. ∎
Formalization notes (this exact statement was proved in a scratch build from the four siblings' exact types): after `obtain ⟨S'', rfl, hS''im⟩` from blowup_preimage use W := dilation x λ ⁻¹' W'; for SameBoundary do `cases n` and in the successor case `show S''.boundary = T.boundary; apply hinj; rw [← hbdry, ← hbdry]; exact hS'bd`; do not rewrite dilation x λ inside types (the domain of blowUp depends on it) — prove compactness of preimages with a separate lemma about an arbitrary compact K and the homeomorphism (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ⁻¹ _).trans (Homeomorph.addLeft (−(λ⁻¹ • x))); rewrite the masses with explicitly instantiated mass_scaling (… P n U T x λ hlam and … P n U S'' x λ hlam) to avoid an unassigned `0 < λ` side goal from rw; close with gcongr.
proof_key_steps: η_#T is integer multiplicity by rep_pushforward.
Given a competitor S' for η_#T on W' ⊂⊂ η(U), take S'' with η_#S'' = S' integer multiplicity (blowup_preimage) and W := η⁻¹(W') ⊂⊂ U.
SameBoundary S'' T and spt(S'' − T) = η⁻¹(spt(S' − η_#T)) compact ⊆ A ∩ W by blowup_structure (i)–(iv).
Minimality of T and mass_scaling give M_{W'}(η_#T) = λ^{−n}M_W(T) ≤ λ^{−n}M_W(S'') = M_{W'}(S').
